source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֣י מ֔וֹת שְׁנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֑ן בְּקָרְבָתָ֥ם לִפְנֵי־יְהוָ֖ה וַיָּמֻֽתוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses after [the] death of [the] two sons of Aaron, when they drew near before Yahweh and died.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they drew near before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and died.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses after Aaron's two sons had come near to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and died.
en.R: Aaron's two sons had died when they came too close to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. After that, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses.

decisions.choice: after the death of the two sons of Aaron: the deaths of Nadab and Abihu in 10:1-2
decisions.reason: The chapter opens by tying itself to the day Nadab and Abihu brought fire God had not commanded and were consumed by fire from before Yahweh (10:1-2). Chapters 11-15 come between, but the instructions for this day answer the danger shown there: how the high priest may come near God's presence and not die (verses 2 and 13). The deaths are recalled again in Numbers 3:4.

decisions.choice: when they drew near before Yahweh: the Hebrew text does not name what they offered
alternatives: when they offered strange fire before Yahweh
decisions.reason: The Westminster Leningrad Codex says only that they "drew near before Yahweh". The Septuagint adds that they offered strange fire, as in 10:1, which is probably an explanation drawn from that verse. The Hebrew is followed here, and the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: drew near: came into God's presence, as a priest does to serve
decisions.reason: "Draw near" is the verb used for approaching God in worship and for bringing an offering (the same root as "offering", 1:2). Here it stands for their unpermitted approach in 10:1. The text says only that they drew near and died; chapter 10 shows what was wrong with their approach.

decisions.choice: Aaron's two sons had died when they came too close ... After that
decisions.reason: Readable tells the background first, in its own sentence, and then says that the LORD spoke. "Too close" is supplied to show the connection with chapter 10.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה דַּבֵּר֮ אֶל־אַהֲרֹ֣ן אָחִיךָ֒ וְאַל־יָבֹ֤א בְכָל־עֵת֙ אֶל־הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ מִבֵּ֖ית לַפָּרֹ֑כֶת אֶל־פְּנֵ֨י הַכַּפֹּ֜רֶת אֲשֶׁ֤ר עַל־הָאָרֹן֙ וְלֹ֣א יָמ֔וּת כִּ֚י בֶּֽעָנָ֔ן אֵרָאֶ֖ה עַל־הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, speak to Aaron your brother, and let him not come at every time into the holy [place] from inside to the veil, to [the] face of the cover which [is] on the ark, and he will not die, for in the cloud I will appear over the cover.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Speak to Aaron your brother, that he not come at any time into the holy place inside the veil, before the cover which [is] on the ark, so that he does not die; for in the cloud I appear over the cover.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Speak to your brother Aaron. He may not go at any time he pleases into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain, before the mercy seat that is on the ark, so that he will not die. For it is in the cloud above the mercy seat that I appear.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Give your brother Aaron this warning. He must not go into the Most Holy Place whenever he likes. That is the room behind the curtain, where the cover of the ark is. If he goes in at the wrong time, he will die. For I appear in the cloud above the cover of the ark.

decisions.choice: the cover: the gold lid on the ark, the place of God's presence and of atonement
decisions.reason: The ark was a wooden chest covered with gold, holding the tablets of the covenant (Exodus 25:10-16). On it lay a slab of pure gold with two gold cherubim, one at each end, their wings spread over it (Exodus 25:17-21). God said, "There I will meet with you" and speak from above it, between the cherubim (Exodus 25:22; Numbers 7:89). Its name comes from the same root as "make atonement", and on this day the blood of the sin offerings is sprinkled on it and in front of it (verses 14-15). The Septuagint uses a word meaning "place of atonement", the word used of Christ in Romans 3:25 and of the ark's lid in Hebrews 9:5.

decisions.choice: the holy place inside the veil: the inner room of the tent, where the ark stood
decisions.reason: The tent had two rooms divided by a curtain: the holy place, with the lampstand, the table and the incense altar, and behind the curtain the most holy place, which held the ark (Exodus 26:31-34). In this chapter "the holy place" usually means that inner room, as "inside the veil" and "before the cover" make plain here, and it is set apart from the rest of "the tent of meeting" in verses 16, 17 and 20. Hebrews 9:7 describes the high priest entering it once a year.

decisions.choice: in the cloud I appear: God's presence shows itself in the cloud above the ark
alternatives: in the cloud of incense I will appear
I will appear in the cloud
decisions.reason: The cloud is most likely the cloud of God's own presence, which covered the tent and filled it with glory (Exodus 40:34-38) and from which he spoke (Numbers 11:25). Some take it as the cloud of incense that Aaron is to make (verse 13), which keeps him from looking at the place where God appears. The verb can be read as a present ("I appear") or a future ("I will appear"). Either way, the reason given is that God himself is present above the cover, so no one may come there except as he directs.

decisions.choice: at any time: not whenever he chooses, but only at the time God sets
decisions.reason: The phrase is literally "at every time". It does not forbid all entry; it limits it to the day and the way the rest of the chapter lays down, "once in the year" (verse 34; Exodus 30:10).

decisions.choice: the Most Holy Place behind the curtain; the mercy seat (Balanced); the cover of the ark (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the holy place", "the veil" and "the cover". Balanced and Readable say "the Most Holy Place" because the inner room is meant, and "the curtain". Balanced keeps the familiar "mercy seat", the name William Tyndale gave it in 1530; Readable says what it is, "the cover of the ark", and adds a sentence saying where the room is.

source.text: בְּזֹ֛את יָבֹ֥א אַהֲרֹ֖ן אֶל־הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ בְּפַ֧ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֛ר לְחַטָּ֖את וְאַ֥יִל לְעֹלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: With this will come Aaron into the holy [place]: with [a] bull, [a] young one of [the] herd, for [a] sin offering, and [a] ram for [a] burnt offering.

en.L: With this Aaron shall come into the holy place: with a bull, a young one of the herd, for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering.
en.B: Aaron may enter the Most Holy Place only in this way: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.
en.R: Here is how Aaron must come into the Most Holy Place. He must bring a young bull as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering.

decisions.choice: with this: in the following way, with the following offerings
decisions.reason: "This" points forward to everything the chapter goes on to describe: the offerings, the clothing (verse 4), and the rites of verses 5-28. Aaron may enter only in this way.

decisions.choice: a bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering: Aaron's own offerings, for himself and his household
decisions.reason: These animals are Aaron's own (verses 6, 11, 24). The bull is the sin offering required for the anointed priest (4:3); the people provide their own goats and ram (verse 5). On "sin offering" see 4:3, and on "burnt offering" see 1:3.

source.text: כְּתֹֽנֶת־בַּ֨ד קֹ֜דֶשׁ יִלְבָּ֗שׁ וּמִֽכְנְסֵי־בַד֮ יִהְי֣וּ עַל־בְּשָׂרוֹ֒ וּבְאַבְנֵ֥ט בַּד֙ יַחְגֹּ֔ר וּבְמִצְנֶ֥פֶת בַּ֖ד יִצְנֹ֑ף בִּגְדֵי־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הֵ֔ם וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֛יִם אֶת־בְּשָׂר֖וֹ וּלְבֵשָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] tunic of linen, holy, he will wear, and undergarments of linen will be on his flesh, and with [a] sash of linen he will gird [himself], and with [a] turban of linen he will wind [himself]; garments of holiness they [are], and he will wash with water his flesh and put them on.

en.L: A holy linen tunic he shall put on, and linen undergarments shall be on his flesh, and with a linen sash he shall tie [himself], and with a linen turban he shall wrap [his head]. They [are] holy garments; and he shall wash his flesh with water and put them on.
en.B: He must be dressed in the holy linen tunic, with linen undergarments on his body, a linen sash tied around him and a linen turban wound on his head. Because these garments are holy, he is to wash his body in water and then put them on.
en.R: He must wear the holy linen tunic and linen underwear. He must tie on a linen sash and wrap a linen turban around his head. These clothes are holy. So he must first wash his body with water and then get dressed.

decisions.choice: linen garments: plain white linen, not the high priest's garments of gold and colored yarn
decisions.reason: On other days the high priest wore garments "for glory and for beauty": the ephod, the breastpiece with its stones, the blue robe and the gold plate (Exodus 28; 8:7-9). For this day he wears only linen, much like the clothing of the ordinary priests (Exodus 28:39-42; 39:27-29). The text does not give the reason. It may show humility before God as he comes to make atonement for himself and the people; linen is also the clothing of heavenly figures in Ezekiel 9:2 and Daniel 10:5. He takes these garments off again after the rite inside (verse 23).

decisions.choice: holy garments: clothing set apart for this service alone
decisions.reason: "Garments of holiness" means clothing that belongs to God's service and may be used for nothing else (Exodus 28:2, 4). Because they are holy, Aaron must wash before he puts them on (Exodus 30:20; 40:31-32).

decisions.choice: his flesh: his body
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means the body: the undergarments are worn next to the skin (as in 6:3), and he is to wash his whole body, not only his hands and feet (compare Exodus 30:19-21).

decisions.choice: next to his body; bathe his body (Balanced); take a bath (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "flesh". Balanced and Readable say "body", and Readable puts the bath first because it comes before he dresses.

source.text: וּמֵאֵ֗ת עֲדַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יִקַּ֛ח שְׁנֵֽי־שְׂעִירֵ֥י עִזִּ֖ים לְחַטָּ֑את וְאַ֥יִל אֶחָ֖ד לְעֹלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And from [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel he will take two male goats of [the] goats for [a] sin offering, and one ram for [a] burnt offering.

en.L: And from the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel he shall take two male goats for a sin offering, and one ram for a burnt offering.
en.B: From the congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} he is to take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
en.R: The people of the community of Israel must give him two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.

decisions.choice: two male goats for a sin offering: the two goats together make the people's sin offering
decisions.reason: Both goats are taken "for a sin offering". Only one is killed (verses 9, 15); the other carries the people's sins away alive (verses 10, 21-22). Together they deal with the people's sin in two ways: by blood brought before God, and by removal far from the camp.

decisions.choice: from the congregation: the people supply these animals, as Aaron supplies his own
decisions.reason: Aaron's bull and ram are for himself and his household (verse 3); these animals come from the people as a whole and are offered for them (verses 15, 24). A male goat is the sin offering for a leader in 4:23, but here it is for all the people (compare 9:3).

decisions.choice: The people ... must give him
decisions.reason: Readable makes the people the subject, which says the same thing more simply than "he shall take from the congregation".

source.text: וְהִקְרִ֧יב אַהֲרֹ֛ן אֶת־פַּ֥ר הַחַטָּ֖את אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ וְכִפֶּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וּבְעַ֥ד בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will present Aaron the bull of the sin offering which [is] for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his household.

en.L: And Aaron shall present the bull of the sin offering which [is] for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his household.
en.B: Aaron is to bring forward the bull that is the sin offering for himself, and so make atonement for himself and those of his household.
en.R: Aaron must bring the bull as a sin offering for himself. In this way he will make atonement for himself and his family.

decisions.choice: his household: his family, including his sons the priests
decisions.reason: "House" means his family. Since his sons serve as priests with him, atonement for his household covers the priesthood, as verse 33 says: "for the priests". The priest who makes atonement for others must first have atonement made for himself (Hebrews 5:3; 7:27).

decisions.choice: present ... and make atonement: a summary, carried out step by step in verses 11-14
decisions.reason: Verses 6-10 give an outline of the day: Aaron's bull (verse 6), the two goats and the lots (verses 7-10). Verses 11-28 then describe each step in order, starting again with the same words about the bull (verse 11).

source.text: וְלָקַ֖ח אֶת־שְׁנֵ֣י הַשְּׂעִירִ֑ם וְהֶעֱמִ֤יד אֹתָם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will take the two male goats and station them before Yahweh [at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting.

en.L: And he shall take the two male goats and set them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [at] the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.B: He is to take the two goats and have them stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.R: He must take the two goats and stand them in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the entrance of the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: set them before Yahweh at the entrance: present both goats to God before the lot is cast
decisions.reason: Both goats are first presented to Yahweh at the entrance of the tent, where offerings are brought (1:3). The goat that will be sent away is also "set alive before Yahweh" (verse 10). Both belong to God's appointed rite before the lot decides their parts.

source.text: וְנָתַ֧ן אַהֲרֹ֛ן עַל־שְׁנֵ֥י הַשְּׂעִירִ֖ם גּוֹרָל֑וֹת גּוֹרָ֤ל אֶחָד֙ לַיהוָ֔ה וְגוֹרָ֥ל אֶחָ֖ד לַעֲזָאזֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And will put Aaron on the two male goats lots: one lot for Yahweh and one lot for Azazel.

en.L: And Aaron shall put lots on the two male goats, one lot for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and one lot for Azazel.
en.B: Over the two goats Aaron is to cast two lots, one lot for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and one lot for Azazel.
en.R: Aaron must use lots to choose between the two goats. One lot is for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the other lot is for Azazel.

decisions.choice: Azazel: a name of unknown meaning, kept as a name
decisions.reason: The word is found only in this chapter (verses 8, 10, 26). Since the lots are "for Yahweh" and "for Azazel", it reads most naturally as a name standing opposite Yahweh's, perhaps of a being thought to live in the wilderness, where goat-demons were believed to dwell (17:7; Isaiah 13:21; 34:14). In the later Book of Enoch, which is not part of Scripture, Azazel is the name of a leader of fallen angels. Others explain the word as "the goat that goes away", which is how the Septuagint and the Latin Vulgate took it, and from which comes the traditional name "scapegoat". Later Jewish tradition took it as the name of a rugged place in the wilderness. Whatever it means, the goat is not an offering to Azazel: both goats are presented to Yahweh (verse 7), and the goat sent away takes Israel's sins to a place cut off from God's people (verse 22).

decisions.choice: lots: a means of letting God decide
decisions.reason: Lots were small objects drawn or cast to reach a decision, in the belief that God directs the outcome (Proverbs 16:33). The land was later divided by lot (Numbers 26:55). Here the lot shows which goat God claims for the sin offering, so Aaron does not choose.

decisions.choice: use lots to choose between the two goats
decisions.reason: Readable says what the lots were for, since "put lots on" would not be clear to a young reader.

source.text: וְהִקְרִ֤יב אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶת־הַשָּׂעִ֔יר אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָלָ֥ה עָלָ֛יו הַגּוֹרָ֖ל לַיהוָ֑ה וְעָשָׂ֖הוּ חַטָּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And will present Aaron the male goat which came up on it the lot for Yahweh, and offer it [as a] sin offering.

en.L: And Aaron shall present the male goat on which the lot for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came up, and offer it [as] a sin offering.
en.B: Aaron is then to bring forward the goat picked by the lot for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and offer it as a sin offering.
en.R: Aaron must bring the goat picked by the lot for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He must offer it as a sin offering.

decisions.choice: on which the lot came up: the goat the lot marked out
decisions.reason: The lot "comes up" or "goes out" for the one chosen (Joshua 18:11; 19:1). The idiom does not say how lots were cast, only that one goat was marked out for Yahweh.

source.text: וְהַשָּׂעִ֗יר אֲשֶׁר֩ עָלָ֨ה עָלָ֤יו הַגּוֹרָל֙ לַעֲזָאזֵ֔ל יָֽעֳמַד־חַ֛י לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְכַפֵּ֣ר עָלָ֑יו לְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֹת֛וֹ לַעֲזָאזֵ֖ל הַמִּדְבָּֽרָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the male goat which came up on it the lot for Azazel will be stationed alive before Yahweh, to make atonement on it, to send it away to Azazel into the wilderness.

en.L: And the male goat on which the lot for Azazel came up shall be set alive before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to make atonement on it, to send it away to Azazel into the wilderness.
en.B: The goat picked by the lot for Azazel, however, is to be set alive before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so that atonement may be made with it by sending it off into the wilderness to Azazel.
en.R: The other goat, picked by the lot for Azazel, must be kept alive and brought in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It has a part in making atonement. It will be sent away into the desert to Azazel.

decisions.choice: to make atonement on it: to use the live goat in the rite of atonement
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual: atonement is normally made "for" people or "on" the altar. Here the live goat itself is the means. Verses 21-22 explain how: Aaron confesses the people's sins over it and it carries them away. Some take the phrase to mean that the goat itself is first purified, but nothing in the rite does that to it.

decisions.choice: to send it away to Azazel: see verse 8
decisions.reason: On the name Azazel see verse 8. The sending away into the wilderness is described in verses 21-22.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: the dry, empty land beyond the camp
decisions.reason: The wilderness is land where few people live and little grows. Verse 22 calls it "a land cut off". Sending the goat there takes the sins far from the camp, where God dwells among his people (verse 16).

decisions.choice: so that atonement may be made with it (Balanced); it has a part in making atonement; desert (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how the goat serves in the atonement, since "make atonement on it" is hard to follow. Readable says "desert" for the wilderness.

source.text: וְהִקְרִ֨יב אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת־פַּ֤ר הַֽחַטָּאת֙ אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ וְכִפֶּ֥ר בַּֽעֲד֖וֹ וּבְעַ֣ד בֵּית֑וֹ וְשָׁחַ֛ט אֶת־פַּ֥ר הַֽחַטָּ֖את אֲשֶׁר־לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will present Aaron the bull of the sin offering which [is] for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his household, and he will slaughter the bull of the sin offering which [is] for himself.

en.L: And Aaron shall present the bull of the sin offering which [is] for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his household; and he shall slaughter the bull of the sin offering which [is] for himself.
en.B: Aaron is to bring forward the bull of his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household. He is to slaughter this bull.
en.R: Aaron must bring the bull as a sin offering for himself. It is to make atonement for himself and his family. He must kill the bull.

decisions.choice: present ... and slaughter: the rite now begins in order, repeating verse 6
decisions.reason: The words of verse 6 are repeated as the detailed account begins. The slaughter of the bull is the first act; its blood is taken inside the curtain in verse 14, after the incense of verses 12-13.

decisions.choice: He is to slaughter this bull (Balanced); He must kill the bull (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "the bull of the sin offering which is for himself" in full. Balanced shortens the repetition, and Readable leaves it out, since the bull has just been named.

source.text: וְלָקַ֣ח מְלֹֽא־הַ֠מַּחְתָּה גַּֽחֲלֵי־אֵ֞שׁ מֵעַ֤ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וּמְלֹ֣א חָפְנָ֔יו קְטֹ֥רֶת סַמִּ֖ים דַּקָּ֑ה וְהֵבִ֖יא מִבֵּ֥ית לַפָּרֹֽכֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will take [the] fullness of the censer, coals of fire from on the altar from before Yahweh, and [the] fullness of his hollow hands [of] incense of spices, fine, and bring [them] from inside to the veil.

en.L: And he shall take a censer full of coals of fire from on the altar, from before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and his two hands full of finely ground fragrant incense, and bring [them] inside the veil.
en.B: He is to fill a censer with burning coals from the altar that stands before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, take two handfuls of fragrant incense ground fine, and carry them in behind the curtain.
en.R: He must fill a fire pan with burning coals from the altar in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He must also take two handfuls of sweet-smelling incense, ground into fine powder. He must bring them into the room behind the curtain.

decisions.choice: coals of fire from the altar: fire taken from the altar of burnt offering, which God himself had lit
decisions.reason: The coals come "from on the altar, from before Yahweh", most likely the altar of burnt offering in the courtyard, whose fire had come from Yahweh (9:24) and was never to go out (6:6). Using fire from this altar, and no other, is the opposite of the "strange fire" of 10:1.

decisions.choice: his two hands full of fine fragrant incense: two handfuls of the sacred incense
decisions.reason: The word for hands means the two hollowed palms held together. The incense is the blend of fragrant spices made for the sanctuary alone and ground fine (Exodus 30:34-38). On "censer" see 10:1.

decisions.choice: a fire pan; the room behind the curtain
decisions.reason: Readable says "fire pan" for the censer, as in 10:1, and "the room behind the curtain" for "inside the veil".

source.text: וְנָתַ֧ן אֶֽת־הַקְּטֹ֛רֶת עַל־הָאֵ֖שׁ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְכִסָּ֣ה׀עֲנַ֣ן הַקְּטֹ֗רֶת אֶת־הַכַּפֹּ֛רֶת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הָעֵד֖וּת וְלֹ֥א יָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will put the incense on the fire before Yahweh, and will cover [the] cloud of the incense the cover which [is] on the testimony, and he will not die.

en.L: And he shall put the incense on the fire before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the cloud of the incense shall cover the cover which [is] on the testimony, so that he does not die.
en.B: There before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} he is to lay the incense on the fire, and the cloud of incense will cover the mercy seat above the testimony. So he will not die.
en.R: There, in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, he must put the incense on the fire. Then the smoke of the incense will hide the cover on the covenant box. That way he will not die.

decisions.choice: the cloud of the incense shall cover the cover: the smoke screens the place where God appears
decisions.reason: The incense makes a thick cloud of smoke that covers the gold lid of the ark, where God appears (verse 2). The text gives the reason in one phrase: "so that he does not die". No one may see God and live (Exodus 33:20), so the high priest enters veiled in smoke. The incense may also be a fitting gift to God as the priest comes into his presence (Psalm 141:2).

decisions.choice: the testimony: the two stone tablets of the covenant, kept in the ark
decisions.reason: God told Moses to put "the testimony" in the ark (Exodus 25:16, 21). It is the two tablets on which the Ten Commandments were written, called "the tablets of the testimony" (Exodus 31:18; 34:29), because they bear witness to the covenant between God and Israel. For this reason the ark is called "the ark of the testimony" (Exodus 25:22), and here "the testimony" stands for the ark itself.

decisions.choice: the smoke of the incense; the covenant box
decisions.reason: Readable says "smoke" for the cloud and "the covenant box" for the testimony, saying what it was. Literal and Balanced keep "the testimony".

source.text: וְלָקַח֙ מִדַּ֣ם הַפָּ֔ר וְהִזָּ֧ה בְאֶצְבָּע֛וֹ עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַכַּפֹּ֖רֶת קֵ֑דְמָה וְלִפְנֵ֣י הַכַּפֹּ֗רֶת יַזֶּ֧ה שֶֽׁבַע־פְּעָמִ֛ים מִן־הַדָּ֖ם בְּאֶצְבָּעֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will take some of [the] blood of the bull and sprinkle with his finger on [the] face of the cover eastward, and before the cover he will sprinkle seven times some of the blood with his finger.

en.L: And he shall take some of the blood of the bull and sprinkle [it] with his finger on the front of the cover, on the east side; and before the cover he shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.
en.B: Some of the bull's blood he is to take and sprinkle with his finger on the east side of the mercy seat, on its front. In front of the mercy seat, too, he is to sprinkle some of the blood with his finger, seven times.
en.R: He must take some of the bull's blood. With his finger he must sprinkle it on the front of the cover of the ark, on the east side. Then he must sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times in front of the cover.

decisions.choice: on the front of the cover, on the east side: on the side facing the priest as he enters
decisions.reason: The tent faced east, so the priest entered from the east and faced west toward the ark. "Eastward" names the side of the cover nearest him. The blood is put on the cover itself and then sprinkled seven times on the ground in front of it.

decisions.choice: sprinkle the blood seven times: the strongest act of cleansing in the law
decisions.reason: In the sin offering for the priest or the whole people, blood is sprinkled seven times before the curtain (4:6, 17). Here it goes further, inside the curtain to the cover itself, the nearest point to God's presence. Seven is the number of completeness. On "sprinkle" see 4:6.

source.text: וְשָׁחַ֞ט אֶת־שְׂעִ֤יר הַֽחַטָּאת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָעָ֔ם וְהֵבִיא֙ אֶת־דָּמ֔וֹ אֶל־מִבֵּ֖ית לַפָּרֹ֑כֶת וְעָשָׂ֣ה אֶת־דָּמ֗וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ לְדַ֣ם הַפָּ֔ר וְהִזָּ֥ה אֹת֛וֹ עַל־הַכַּפֹּ֖רֶת וְלִפְנֵ֥י הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will slaughter [the] male goat of the sin offering which [is] for the people, and bring its blood to from inside to the veil, and do with its blood just as he did with the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it on the cover and before the cover.

en.L: And he shall slaughter the male goat of the sin offering which [is] for the people, and bring its blood inside the veil, and do with its blood just as he did with the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it on the cover and before the cover.
en.B: Then he is to slaughter the goat that is the sin offering for the people and bring its blood inside the curtain. He is to do with this blood what he did with the bull's blood, sprinkling it on the mercy seat and before it.
en.R: Next he must kill the goat that is the sin offering for the people. He must bring its blood into the room behind the curtain. He must do with it just what he did with the bull's blood. He must sprinkle it on the cover of the ark and in front of it.

decisions.choice: the goat of the sin offering which is for the people: the goat chosen by the lot for Yahweh
decisions.reason: This is the goat of verse 9. After Aaron's own sin offering has made atonement for him and the priests, the same rite is done for the people.

source.text: וְכִפֶּ֣ר עַל־הַקֹּ֗דֶשׁ מִטֻּמְאֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמִפִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֖ם לְכָל־חַטֹּאתָ֑ם וְכֵ֤ן יַעֲשֶׂה֙ לְאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד הַשֹּׁכֵ֣ן אִתָּ֔ם בְּת֖וֹךְ טֻמְאֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will make atonement on the holy [place] from the uncleannesses of [the] sons of Israel and from their transgressions, for all their sins; and so he will do for [the] tent of meeting, which dwells with them in [the] midst of their uncleannesses.

en.L: And he shall make atonement for the holy place, because of the uncleannesses of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and because of their transgressions, all their sins; and so he shall do for the tent of meeting, which dwells with them in the midst of their uncleannesses.
en.B: So he will make atonement for the Most Holy Place, cleansing it from the impurities of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, from their rebellious acts and all their sins. He is to do the same for the tent of meeting, which stays with them right among their impurities.
en.R: In this way he will make atonement for the Most Holy Place. It must be made clean from the unclean things the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have done, from all their sins and their turning against God. He must do the same for the rest of the meeting tent. It stands among the people, even though they are unclean.

decisions.choice: make atonement for the holy place: cleanse the sanctuary itself of the people's uncleanness
decisions.reason: Here atonement is made not for people but for a place. The uncleanness and sins of Israel defile the sanctuary where God dwells (15:31; 20:3), even when it is far from the sinner. Once a year the blood cleanses it, so that God may go on living among his people. Verse 19 uses the plain verbs: "purify it and make it holy".

decisions.choice: uncleannesses, transgressions, sins: every kind of wrong and defilement
decisions.reason: Three words together cover the whole range. "Uncleannesses" are the impurities of chapters 11-15. "Transgressions" are acts of rebellion, deliberate breaking away from God (the word is used of a vassal's revolt, 2 Kings 8:20). "Sins" is the general word for doing wrong. The day deals with all of them, the deliberate as well as the unintentional (compare 4:2).

decisions.choice: the tent of meeting, which dwells with them: the tent where God lives among them
decisions.reason: The participle "dwells" is used of the tent, but it is God who dwells in it (Exodus 25:8; 29:45). After the inner room, the same rite of blood is done for the outer room of the tent, which stands in the middle of an unclean people.

decisions.choice: impurities; rebellious acts (Balanced); unclean things ... turning against God (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "uncleannesses" and "transgressions". Balanced uses "impurities" and "rebellious acts". Readable explains them in common words and calls the outer room "the rest of the meeting tent".

source.text: וְכָל־אָדָ֞ם לֹא־יִהְיֶ֣ה׀בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֗ד בְּבֹא֛וֹ לְכַפֵּ֥ר בַּקֹּ֖דֶשׁ עַד־צֵאת֑וֹ וְכִפֶּ֤ר בַּעֲדוֹ֙ וּבְעַ֣ד בֵּית֔וֹ וּבְעַ֖ד כָּל־קְהַ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And any person not will be in [the] tent of meeting when he goes to make atonement in the holy [place] until he comes out; and he will make atonement for himself and for his household and for all [the] assembly of Israel.

en.L: And no one shall be in the tent of meeting when he goes in to make atonement in the holy place, until he comes out; and he shall make atonement for himself and for his household and for all the assembly of Israel.
en.B: While Aaron is inside making atonement in the Most Holy Place, no one may be in the tent of meeting until he comes out again. He makes atonement for himself, for his household and for the whole assembly of Israel.
en.R: No one else may be in the meeting tent when Aaron goes into the Most Holy Place to make atonement. They must stay out until he comes out again. He will make atonement for himself, for his family and for all the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: no one: no human being at all, not even another priest
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being. Not even the priests who normally serve in the outer room may be inside while Aaron makes atonement. He alone goes in.

decisions.choice: all the assembly of Israel: the whole people gathered as God's community
decisions.reason: The "assembly" is Israel as a people gathered before God. The atonement Aaron makes covers three circles in turn: himself, his household of priests, and the whole nation.

decisions.choice: Aaron
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he". Balanced and Readable name Aaron so that "he" is not taken to mean the "no one" of the first clause.

source.text: וְיָצָ֗א אֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֛חַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִפְנֵֽי־יְהוָ֖ה וְכִפֶּ֣ר עָלָ֑יו וְלָקַ֞ח מִדַּ֤ם הַפָּר֙ וּמִדַּ֣ם הַשָּׂעִ֔יר וְנָתַ֛ן עַל־קַרְנ֥וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will go out to the altar which [is] before Yahweh and make atonement on it, and he will take some of [the] blood of the bull and some of [the] blood of the male goat and put [it] on [the] horns of the altar all around.

en.L: And he shall go out to the altar which [is] before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and make atonement for it; and he shall take some of the blood of the bull and some of the blood of the male goat and put [it] on the horns of the altar all around.
en.B: Next he is to go out to the altar before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and make atonement for it. Taking some of the blood of the bull and of the goat, he is to put it on the horns of the altar on every side.
en.R: Then he must go out to the altar in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and make atonement for it. He must take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood. He must put it on all the corners of the altar that stick up like horns.

decisions.choice: the altar which is before Yahweh: most likely the altar of burnt offering in the courtyard
decisions.reason: Aaron "goes out" to this altar, which suggests he leaves the tent for the altar of burnt offering in the courtyard, the third part of the sanctuary in verses 20 and 33. Others take it as the gold incense altar just outside the curtain, since Exodus 30:10 says atonement is to be made on its horns once a year with the blood of the sin offering, and 4:7 calls that altar "before Yahweh".

decisions.choice: the horns of the altar: the projections at its four corners
decisions.reason: The altar had a horn-shaped projection at each corner (Exodus 27:2). Blood on the horns is part of the sin offering rite (4:7, 25; 8:15).

decisions.choice: the corners of the altar that stick up like horns
decisions.reason: Readable explains "horns", which could otherwise be taken as animal horns.

source.text: וְהִזָּ֨ה עָלָ֧יו מִן־הַדָּ֛ם בְּאֶצְבָּע֖וֹ שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֑ים וְטִהֲר֣וֹ וְקִדְּשׁ֔וֹ מִטֻּמְאֹ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will sprinkle on it some of the blood with his finger seven times, and purify it and make it holy from the uncleannesses of [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And he shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, and purify it and consecrate it from the uncleannesses of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: He is to sprinkle some of the blood on the altar with his finger seven times. So he will purify it from the impurities of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and make it holy again.
en.R: With his finger he must sprinkle some of the blood on the altar seven times. That will make it clean and holy again, free from the unclean things the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have done.

decisions.choice: purify it and consecrate it: take away its uncleanness and restore it to holy use
decisions.reason: The first verb is the one behind "sin offering" and means to cleanse from sin or impurity (8:15). The second means to make holy, set apart for God (8:10-11). The altar is not only cleaned but given back to God's service.

decisions.choice: make it holy again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "again", since the altar was already consecrated (8:11) and is now restored. Literal says "consecrate it".

source.text: וְכִלָּה֙ מִכַּפֵּ֣ר אֶת־הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וְאֶת־אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד וְאֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְהִקְרִ֖יב אֶת־הַשָּׂעִ֥יר הֶחָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will finish making atonement for the holy [place] and the tent of meeting and the altar, and he will present the male goat, the living [one].

en.L: And when he has finished making atonement for the holy place and the tent of meeting and the altar, he shall present the living male goat.
en.B: Once he has completed the atonement for the Most Holy Place, the tent of meeting and the altar, he is to present the goat that is still alive.
en.R: Aaron will finish making atonement for the Most Holy Place, the rest of the meeting tent and the altar. Then he must bring the goat that is still alive.

decisions.choice: the holy place, the tent of meeting and the altar: the three parts of the sanctuary, from the inside out
decisions.reason: Aaron cleanses the sanctuary in order from God's presence outward: the inner room (verses 14-16a), the rest of the tent (verse 16b), and the altar (verses 18-19). The same three are named in verse 33.

source.text: וְסָמַ֨ךְ אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת־שְׁתֵּ֣י יָדָ֗יו עַ֨ל רֹ֣אשׁ הַשָּׂעִיר֮ הַחַי֒ וְהִתְוַדָּ֣ה עָלָ֗יו אֶת־כָּל־עֲוֺנֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶת־כָּל־פִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֖ם לְכָל־חַטֹּאתָ֑ם וְנָתַ֤ן אֹתָם֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הַשָּׂעִ֔יר וְשִׁלַּ֛ח בְּיַד־אִ֥ישׁ עִתִּ֖י הַמִּדְבָּֽרָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will lean Aaron his two hands on [the] head of the male goat, the living [one], and confess over it all [the] iniquities of [the] sons of Israel and all their transgressions, for all their sins, and put them on [the] head of the male goat, and send [it] away by [the] hand of [a] man ready into the wilderness.

en.L: And Aaron shall lean both his hands on the head of the living male goat, and confess over it all the iniquities of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and all their transgressions, all their sins, and he shall put them on the head of the goat and send [it] away into the wilderness by the hand of a man [standing] ready.
en.B: Aaron is to lay both his hands on the live goat's head and confess over it all the wrongdoing of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, all their rebellious acts, all their sins. So he is to place them on the goat's head, and send it off into the wilderness with a man kept ready for that purpose.
en.R: Aaron must put both his hands on the head of the live goat. He must confess over it all the evil the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have done, all their sins and their turning against God. In this way he will put their sins on the goat's head. Then a man chosen for the job must lead the goat away into the desert.

decisions.choice: lean both his hands on the head: transfer the people's sins to the goat
decisions.reason: In other offerings the worshiper leans one hand on the animal (1:4). Here Aaron uses both hands, and the text says what the act means: he "puts" the sins on the goat's head. Confession aloud goes with the gesture, as it does with the guilt of 5:5.

decisions.choice: confess ... iniquities, transgressions, sins: name aloud every kind of guilt
decisions.reason: "Iniquities" are wrongs seen as guilt that weighs on the one who did them; the goat "bears" them in verse 22, as a guilty person bears his iniquity (5:1). With "transgressions" and "sins" (see verse 16) the list leaves nothing out.

decisions.choice: a man standing ready: a man appointed in advance for the task
decisions.reason: The second word is found only here. It is related to the word for "time", so it means a man ready at the right time, kept on hand to lead the goat away. Later Jewish practice appointed a particular man for this.

decisions.choice: wrongdoing (Balanced); evil (Readable); with a man kept ready for that purpose (Balanced); a man chosen for the job (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "iniquities" and "by the hand of a man ready". Balanced and Readable use common words and say what the man is for.

source.text: וְנָשָׂ֨א הַשָּׂעִ֥יר עָלָ֛יו אֶת־כָּל־עֲוֺנֹתָ֖ם אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ גְּזֵרָ֑ה וְשִׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־הַשָּׂעִ֖יר בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And will bear the male goat on itself all their iniquities to [a] land cut off, and he will let go the male goat in the wilderness.

en.L: And the goat shall bear on itself all their iniquities to a land cut off; and he shall let the goat go in the wilderness.
en.B: The goat will carry all their wrongdoing on itself into a barren land, and the man is to set the goat free in the wilderness.
en.R: The goat will carry all their sins away to a place where no one lives. The man must let the goat go free in the desert.

decisions.choice: the goat shall bear all their iniquities: it carries the guilt of Israel away
decisions.reason: To "bear iniquity" is usually to carry one's own guilt and its penalty (5:1, 17). Here the goat bears the guilt of others and takes it out of the camp. The picture is of sin removed so far that it can never return (Psalm 103:12; Micah 7:19). Isaiah 53:11-12 speaks of the Servant who bears the iniquities of many.

decisions.choice: a land cut off: a remote, barren land from which nothing returns
decisions.reason: The word means cut off or separated. It describes land cut off from human life, either barren or simply isolated, so that the goat, and the sins it carries, cannot come back to the camp.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he". Balanced and Readable name "the man" of verse 21, who leads the goat away, so that the reader does not take it to be Aaron.

source.text: וּבָ֤א אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וּפָשַׁט֙ אֶת־בִּגְדֵ֣י הַבָּ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָבַ֖שׁ בְּבֹא֣וֹ אֶל־הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וְהִנִּיחָ֖ם שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will come Aaron into [the] tent of meeting and strip off the garments of linen which he wore when he went into the holy [place], and leave them there.

en.L: And Aaron shall come into the tent of meeting and take off the linen garments which he put on when he went into the holy place, and he shall leave them there.
en.B: After that Aaron is to go into the tent of meeting. There he is to take off the linen garments he put on to enter the Most Holy Place, and leave them in the tent.
en.R: Then Aaron must go into the meeting tent. He must take off the linen clothes he wore to go into the Most Holy Place. He must leave them there.

decisions.choice: take off the linen garments and leave them there: the clothing of the inner rite stays in the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The linen garments (verse 4) were worn only for entering the inner room. Aaron leaves them inside the tent, and they are not used for anything else. Garments that have come so near to the holy are kept from ordinary use, as in 6:4 (compare Ezekiel 44:19).

source.text: וְרָחַ֨ץ אֶת־בְּשָׂר֤וֹ בַמַּ֨יִם֙ בְּמָק֣וֹם קָד֔וֹשׁ וְלָבַ֖שׁ אֶת־בְּגָדָ֑יו וְיָצָ֗א וְעָשָׂ֤ה אֶת־עֹֽלָתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־עֹלַ֣ת הָעָ֔ם וְכִפֶּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וּבְעַ֥ד הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will wash his flesh with water in [a] holy place and put on his garments, and he will come out and offer his burnt offering and [the] burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people.

en.L: And he shall wash his flesh with water in a holy place and put on his garments, and come out and offer his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people.
en.B: He is to wash his body with water in a holy place and dress in his usual garments. Then he is to come out and offer the burnt offering for himself and the one for the people, making atonement for himself and the people.
en.R: He must take a bath in a holy place and put on his usual priest's clothes. Then he must come out and offer two burnt offerings, one for himself and one for the people. In this way he will make atonement for himself and for the people.

decisions.choice: his garments: his usual high priest's garments
decisions.reason: These are the garments "for glory and for beauty" (Exodus 28:2), the opposite of the plain linen of verse 4. Dressed in them he offers the two rams of verses 3 and 5 as burnt offerings.

decisions.choice: in a holy place: in the courtyard of the sanctuary
decisions.reason: "A holy place" without the article is the courtyard of the tent, where the holy portions are eaten (6:9, 19) and where the basin for washing stood (Exodus 30:18). It is not the inner room.

decisions.choice: his usual garments (Balanced); usual priest's clothes (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which garments are meant, since Aaron has just taken off the linen ones.

source.text: וְאֵ֛ת חֵ֥לֶב הַֽחַטָּ֖את יַקְטִ֥יר הַמִּזְבֵּֽחָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the fat of the sin offering he will make smoke [on] the altar.

en.L: And the fat of the sin offering he shall make smoke on the altar.
en.B: The fat of the sin offering he is to burn on the altar.
en.R: He must burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar too.

decisions.choice: the fat of the sin offering: the fat of both the bull and the goat
decisions.reason: As in every sin offering, the fat is burned on the altar (4:8-10, 19). The rest of the two animals is burned outside the camp (verse 27). On "fat" see 3:3.

source.text: וְהַֽמְשַׁלֵּ֤חַ אֶת־הַשָּׂעִיר֙ לַֽעֲזָאזֵ֔ל יְכַבֵּ֣ס בְּגָדָ֔יו וְרָחַ֥ץ אֶת־בְּשָׂר֖וֹ בַּמָּ֑יִם וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֖ן יָב֥וֹא אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the [one] letting go the male goat to Azazel will wash his garments and wash his flesh with water, and after so he will come into the camp.

en.L: And the one who lets the goat go to Azazel shall wash his garments and wash his flesh with water, and after that he may come into the camp.
en.B: The man who led the goat away to Azazel is to wash his clothes and bathe in water before he comes back into the camp.
en.R: The man who let the goat go to Azazel must wash his clothes and take a bath. After that he may come back into the camp.

decisions.choice: wash ... and after that come into the camp: contact with the goat that bore the sins makes him unclean
decisions.reason: The goat carried Israel's guilt, so the man who led it away must wash before he returns, just like the one who burns the sin offering (verse 28). On Azazel see verse 8.

source.text: וְאֵת֩ פַּ֨ר הַֽחַטָּ֜את וְאֵ֣ת׀שְׂעִ֣יר הַֽחַטָּ֗את אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוּבָ֤א אֶת־דָּמָם֙ לְכַפֵּ֣ר בַּקֹּ֔דֶשׁ יוֹצִ֖יא אֶל־מִח֣וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וְשָׂרְפ֣וּ בָאֵ֔שׁ אֶת־עֹרֹתָ֥ם וְאֶת־בְּשָׂרָ֖ם וְאֶת־פִּרְשָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the bull of the sin offering and the male goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought to make atonement in the holy [place], one will bring out to outside the camp, and they will burn with fire their hides and their flesh and their dung.

en.L: And the bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, one shall bring out to outside the camp, and they shall burn their hides and their flesh and their dung with fire.
en.B: As for the bull and the goat of the sin offerings, whose blood was taken into the Most Holy Place for atonement, someone is to carry them outside the camp, and there their skins, meat and dung are to be burned.
en.R: The blood of the bull and the goat for the sin offerings was brought into the Most Holy Place to make atonement. So the rest of these animals must be taken outside the camp. Their skins, their meat and their dung must be burned up there.

decisions.choice: whose blood was brought into the holy place ... burned outside the camp: these sin offerings may not be eaten
decisions.reason: When the blood of a sin offering is brought inside the tent, its meat is not eaten by the priests but burned outside the camp (4:11-12, 21; 6:23). Hebrews 13:11-12 recalls this rule.

decisions.choice: someone is to carry them ... are to be burned (Balanced); must be taken ... must be burned up (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses "one will bring out" and "they will burn" with no named subject. Balanced uses "someone" and a passive, Readable uses passives, and Readable gives the reason in a sentence of its own.

source.text: וְהַשֹּׂרֵ֣ף אֹתָ֔ם יְכַבֵּ֣ס בְּגָדָ֔יו וְרָחַ֥ץ אֶת־בְּשָׂר֖וֹ בַּמָּ֑יִם וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֖ן יָב֥וֹא אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the [one] burning them will wash his garments and wash his flesh with water, and after so he will come into the camp.

en.L: And the one who burns them shall wash his garments and wash his flesh with water, and after that he may come into the camp.
en.B: The one who burns them is to wash his clothes and bathe in water before he comes back into the camp.
en.R: The man who burns them must wash his clothes and take a bath. After that he may come back into the camp.

decisions.choice: the one who burns them: he too must wash before returning
decisions.reason: The rule is the same as for the man who led away the goat (verse 26). Handling what has carried away the people's sin makes a person unclean.

source.text: וְהָיְתָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לְחֻקַּ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַ֠שְּׁבִיעִי בֶּֽעָשׂ֨וֹר לַחֹ֜דֶשׁ תְּעַנּ֣וּ אֶת־נַפְשֹֽׁתֵיכֶ֗ם וְכָל־מְלָאכָה֙ לֹ֣א תַעֲשׂ֔וּ הָֽאֶזְרָ֔ח וְהַגֵּ֖ר הַגָּ֥ר בְּתוֹכְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be for you [a] statute forever: in the month the seventh, on [the] tenth of the month you will afflict your souls, and any work you will not do, the native and the sojourner who sojourns in your midst.

en.L: And it shall be for you a statute forever: in the seventh month, on the tenth [day] of the month, you shall afflict yourselves and you shall do no work at all, the native and the sojourner who sojourns among you.
en.B: This is to be a permanent rule for you. On the tenth day of the seventh month you are to humble yourselves by fasting and do no work of any kind. This applies to the native-born and to the outsider who lives among you.
en.R: This is a rule for all time. On the tenth day of the seventh month, you must go without food and humble yourselves before God. You must not do any work. This rule is for those born in Israel and for strangers who live among you.

decisions.choice: afflict yourselves: humble yourselves before God, above all by fasting
decisions.reason: Literally "afflict your souls". The phrase means to bring oneself low, and it is used of fasting: "I afflicted my soul with fasting" (Psalm 35:13); "Why have we fasted ... why have we afflicted our souls?" (Isaiah 58:3, 5; compare Ezra 8:21). The same command is given in 23:27-32 and Numbers 29:7, where anyone who does not keep it is cut off. It is the inner response of the people to the atonement made for them: sorrow for sin shown in going without food.

decisions.choice: the sojourner: a foreigner who has come to live among Israel
decisions.reason: A sojourner is someone from another people who has settled in Israel and lives there without the family land and kin of a native. The law protects such people (19:33-34) and in many matters binds them as it binds Israel (17:8, 15; 24:22). Here they too must rest and humble themselves, because the sanctuary in their midst is cleansed for all who live in the camp.

decisions.choice: the tenth day of the seventh month: in early autumn, ten days after the new year's trumpet day
decisions.reason: The seventh month falls in September or October. Its first day is a day of trumpet blasts (23:24), and its fifteenth begins the Festival of Booths (23:34). The tenth day is called the Day of Atonement in 23:27 and 25:9. On "a statute forever" see 3:17.

decisions.choice: humble yourselves by fasting (Balanced); go without food and humble yourselves before God (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "afflict yourselves". Balanced and Readable make the fasting explicit, as Psalm 35:13 and Isaiah 58:3 show it was meant, and keep the sense of humbling oneself.

decisions.choice: the native and the sojourner (Literal); the native-born and the outsider (Balanced); those born in Israel and strangers (Readable)
decisions.reason: These follow the wording used throughout Leviticus (17:15).

source.text: כִּֽי־בַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֛ה יְכַפֵּ֥ר עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם לְטַהֵ֣ר אֶתְכֶ֑ם מִכֹּל֙ חַטֹּ֣אתֵיכֶ֔ם לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה תִּטְהָֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For on the day the this he will make atonement for you, to purify you; from all your sins before Yahweh you will be clean.

en.L: For on this day he shall make atonement for you, to cleanse you; from all your sins before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} you shall be clean.
en.B: For on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you, so that before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} you are clean of all your sins.
en.R: This is the day when atonement will be made for you, to make you clean. Then you will be clean in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, free from all your sins.

decisions.choice: make atonement for you, to cleanse you: atonement wipes away sin like a stain, so that the people are clean
decisions.reason: Here the purpose of atonement is said plainly: "to cleanse you". Sin is pictured as defilement on the people, as uncleanness was on the sanctuary (verses 16, 19). The blood offered before God takes it away, and they become clean. This is the sense of atonement throughout Leviticus: putting right what stands between God and his people by removing the sin that separates them (see 1:4; 17:11). David's prayer "wash me ... cleanse me from my sin" uses the same picture (Psalm 51:4).

decisions.choice: he shall make atonement: the priest makes it, as verse 32 says
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. The priest is the one who makes atonement throughout the chapter (verse 32), so the subject is most likely the priest, or else it is impersonal: "atonement will be made". God is the one who grants it, but the verb is used for the priest's act.

decisions.choice: from all your sins before Yahweh you shall be clean: clean in God's sight
alternatives: from all your sins against Yahweh
decisions.reason: The accents of the Hebrew text join "before Yahweh" to "you shall be clean": the people will be clean in God's presence and in his judgment. It could also be read with "your sins", meaning sins against Yahweh; the sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: atonement will be made for you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a passive for the verb with no stated subject, so as not to suggest a subject the Hebrew does not name.

source.text: שַׁבַּ֨ת שַׁבָּת֥וֹן הִיא֙ לָכֶ֔ם וְעִנִּיתֶ֖ם אֶת־נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶ֑ם חֻקַּ֖ת עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] sabbath of sabbath-rest it [is] for you, and you will afflict your souls; [a] statute forever.

en.L: It [is] a sabbath of rest for you, and you shall afflict yourselves; [it is] a statute forever.
en.B: It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, a day to humble yourselves by fasting. This is a permanent rule.
en.R: It is a day of complete rest for you. You must go without food and humble yourselves. This is a rule for all time.

decisions.choice: a sabbath of rest: a day of the fullest rest, like the weekly Sabbath
decisions.reason: The phrase joins "sabbath" with a related word meaning rest or a sabbath observance, to make it as strong as possible: a day of complete rest. It is used of the weekly Sabbath (23:3; Exodus 31:15; 35:2) and of this day (23:32). On ordinary festival days only ordinary work is forbidden (23:7-8); on this day, as on the weekly Sabbath, no work of any kind may be done (verse 29; 23:28-31).

decisions.choice: afflict yourselves: see verse 29
decisions.reason: The command of verse 29 is repeated: the rest is joined with humbling oneself by fasting.

decisions.choice: a day of complete rest
decisions.reason: Readable says "a day of complete rest", as in the other chapters, because this day is not the seventh day of the week.

source.text: וְכִפֶּ֨ר הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֲשֶׁר־יִמְשַׁ֣ח אֹת֗וֹ וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר יְמַלֵּא֙ אֶת־יָד֔וֹ לְכַהֵ֖ן תַּ֣חַת אָבִ֑יו וְלָבַ֛שׁ אֶת־בִּגְדֵ֥י הַבָּ֖ד בִּגְדֵ֥י הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will make atonement the priest whom one will anoint him and whom one will fill his hand to serve as priest in place of his father, and he will put on the garments of linen, the garments of holiness.

en.L: And the priest who is anointed and who is ordained to serve as priest in place of his father shall make atonement, and he shall put on the linen garments, the holy garments.
en.B: The atonement is to be made by the priest who has been anointed and ordained to serve as priest in his father's place. He is to put on the linen garments, the holy garments,
en.R: In later years, atonement will be made by the priest who is anointed and given his father's place as high priest. He must put on the holy linen clothes.

decisions.choice: anointed and ordained: made high priest in the way of chapter 8
decisions.reason: "Whose hand one fills" is the idiom for ordaining a priest (8:33; Exodus 29:9). Anointing was the sign of the high priest (4:3; 8:12; 21:10). The day is not for Aaron alone: each high priest after him, his son in turn, must keep it.

decisions.choice: who is anointed and ordained: the verbs have no named subject
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "whom one anoints and whose hand one fills", with no subject named. It means simply the one who is anointed and ordained.

decisions.choice: In later years; as high priest
decisions.reason: Readable adds "in later years" and "high priest" to make clear that the rule is for Aaron's successors. The Hebrew says "the priest ... in place of his father".

decisions.choice: the holy garments, (ending with a comma)
decisions.reason: Balanced runs this sentence on into verse 33, since the high priest's atonement in verse 33 is the purpose of putting on the garments.

source.text: וְכִפֶּר֙ אֶת־מִקְדַּ֣שׁ הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וְאֶת־אֹ֧הֶל מוֹעֵ֛ד וְאֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ יְכַפֵּ֑ר וְעַ֧ל הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים וְעַל־כָּל־עַ֥ם הַקָּהָ֖ל יְכַפֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will make atonement for [the] sanctuary of holiness, and [the] tent of meeting and the altar he will make atonement for, and for the priests and for all [the] people of the assembly he will make atonement.

en.L: And he shall make atonement for the holy sanctuary, and for the tent of meeting and for the altar he shall make atonement, and for the priests and for all the people of the assembly he shall make atonement.
en.B: and make atonement for the holy sanctuary, for the tent of meeting and for the altar, and also for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
en.R: He will make atonement for the Most Holy Place, the meeting tent and the altar. He will also make atonement for the priests and for all the people.

decisions.choice: the holy sanctuary: the inner room, the Most Holy Place
decisions.reason: "Sanctuary of holiness" stands first in the list, before "the tent of meeting" and "the altar", as "the holy place" does in verse 20, so it is most likely the inner room. The verse sums up the whole day: atonement for each part of the sanctuary, then for the priests and for the people.

decisions.choice: he shall make atonement, three times: the verb is repeated for emphasis
decisions.reason: The verse uses "make atonement" three times, once for each group: the holy place, the tent and the altar, the priests and the people. The repetition stresses that nothing is left out.

decisions.choice: the holy sanctuary (Balanced); the Most Holy Place (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "the holy sanctuary", the form of the Hebrew, since the wording differs from "the holy place". Readable says "the Most Holy Place", as in the rest of the chapter, and leaves out the repeated verbs.

source.text: וְהָֽיְתָה־זֹּ֨את לָכֶ֜ם לְחֻקַּ֣ת עוֹלָ֗ם לְכַפֵּ֞ר עַל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִכָּל־חַטֹּאתָ֔ם אַחַ֖ת בַּשָּׁנָ֑ה וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it will be this for you [a] statute forever, to make atonement for [the] sons of Israel from all their sins once in the year. And he did just as had commanded Yahweh Moses.

en.L: And this shall be for you a statute forever, to make atonement for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel for all their sins once in the year." And he did just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.
en.B: This is to be a permanent rule for you, that once a year atonement is made for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} for all their sins." And Aaron did as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.
en.R: This is a rule for all time. Once every year atonement must be made for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} for all their sins." And Aaron did everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

decisions.choice: once in the year: a single day each year
decisions.reason: The rite of this chapter is done once a year, on the tenth day of the seventh month (verse 29; Exodus 30:10). Hebrews 9:7, 25 recalls that the high priest entered the inner room only once a year.

decisions.choice: and he did: most likely Aaron, who carried out what God commanded
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. Aaron is the one commanded throughout the chapter, so "he" is most likely Aaron, keeping the day when it came, as Moses had passed on the command. It could also be Moses, who did as commanded by passing these words on to Aaron.

decisions.choice: Aaron
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Aaron as the one who did what was commanded; see the meaning decision. Literal keeps "he".
